content: 1. The maximum recommended daily dose of ezogabine is 1200 mg. When prescribing ezogabine with agents known to prolong the QT interval, careful monitoring of the QT interval is necessary. 2. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Adjust the doses of CYP3A4 substrate drugs as needed. 3. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of finasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium levels during initiation and dosage adjustments of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as necessary. 5. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and flecainide prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 6. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and fluoxetine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of fluvastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Note: OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 9. Both fluvoxamine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and foscarnet prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 11. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Concomitant use of fostamatinib may increase concentrations of P-gp substrates. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrate drugs, and consider dosage reductions when co-administered with fostamatinib. 12. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate through OATP1B1/3 transporter inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 13. Both gadobenate and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and gemtuzumab prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of gentamicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both gepirone and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Goserelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 18. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the FDA recommends reducing the dose to half of the recommended dose if co-administered. No specific recommendations are available for immediate-release guanfacine. 19. Histrelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 20. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. The use of a CYP3A4 inhibitor may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide, potentially reducing its therapeutic effects. 23. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and iloperidone prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 24. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of inhaled indacaterol by modulating P-gp and CYP3A4 activities. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 26. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 and P-gp substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 31. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the ivacaftor dose if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may inhibit P-gp, significantly increasing systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 33. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. Monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 35. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ketoconazole also increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last SC dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 39. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and lenvatinib prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 40. Letermovir increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 42. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema when amlodipine is co-administered with CYP3A inhibitors to determine the need for dose adjustment. 43. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and levofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 44. Levoketoconazole increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate also increases levoketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Lorlatinib decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 49. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases lurasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The manufacturer recommends decreasing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Concurrent use may increase the risk of lurasidone-related adverse reactions. 50. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mavorizxafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for mavorizxafor adverse effects if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Mavorizxafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation (e.g., co-administered medications that increase mavorizxafor exposure or other drugs with a high risk to prolong the QTc interval). 53. Mavorizxafor increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Caution is advised if mavorizxafor (a P-gp inhibitor) is co-administered with a sensitive P-gp substrate where minimal substrate concentration changes may lead to serious adverse effects. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases mestranol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and methadone prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 58. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 60. Both mifepristone and erythromycin ethylsuccinate have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 61. Mitotane decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates for possible dosage adjustments. 62. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases mitoxantrone levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of momelotinib through mechanisms involving OATP1B1/B3 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely.
